blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

The formula is:

CRAP = CC² · (1 − coverage)³ + CC

- `isActiveRun`: CC 5, cov 0 → 25·1 + 5 = 30 ✓
- `classify`: CC 34, cov 0.959 → 1156·(0.041)³ + 34 = 1156·0.000689 + 34 = 0.0797 + 34 = 34.08 ≈ 34.1 ✓
- `orphanedRunChecks`: CC 23, cov 1 → 0 + 23 = 23 ✓
- `collectArtifacts`: CC 8, cov 0.261 → 64·(0.739)³ + 8 = 64·0.4036 + 8 = 25.8 + 8 = 33.8 ✓
- `action` (cacheToReleases): CC 31, cov 0.860 → 961·(0.14)³ + 31 = 961·0.002744 + 31 = 2.637+31 = 33.6 ≈ 33.7 ✓

So the target: CRAP ≤ 8 for each named function.
- With 100% coverage, CRAP = CC. So a function with CC ≤ 8 fully covered gives CRAP ≤ 8. 
- `classify` at CC 34 → need extraction + 100% coverage of each helper; `classify` itself must drop to CC ≤ 8 with 100% coverage (CRAP = CC ≤ 8).

The hard floor is 30 (never above baseline).

Plan per function:

### 1. `checkRunZombies.classify` (CC 34)
Extract the per-check-run decision into pure helpers, e.g.:
- `classifyLinkedRun(cr, runId, resolveRun, nowMs, graceMs)` → verdict object `{kind, zombie}` — handles probe error, no-run, active, completed/canceled/concluded/propagation-lag/odd.
- `classifyUnlinkedRun(cr, nowMs, staleMs)` → verdict — stale-no-runner vs live.
- maybe `completedRunVerdict(state, runId, cr, nowMs, graceMs)`.

Then `classify` becomes: iterate checkRuns, call `isPendingCheckRun` → settled; runIdOf; dispatch to helpers; tally counters. Target CC ≤ 8.

Each helper fully covered by tests. The existing test suite (49 tests) already covers classify thoroughly at 95.9%. After extraction, helpers must be 100% covered. Which branch is currently uncovered? Coverage 95.9% on classify. Let me find uncovered statements: probably `out.live++ // completed without a conclusion` (odd case) or `lag !== null && lag >= 0 && lag <= graceMs` false-negative branch... I'll check coverage detail after refactor. New tests must cover every branch of the helpers.

### 2. `dfManager.isActiveRun` (CC 5, cov 0)
0% coverage! Rewrite as status lookup:
```js
var ACTIVE_RUN_STATUSES = ['queued', 'pending', 'requested', 'waiting', 'in_progress'];
function isActiveRun(run) {
   return ACTIVE_RUN_STATUSES.indexOf(runStatus(run)) !== -1;
}
``
CC becomes 1; CRAP = 1 + 0 = ... CC=1, cov: need coverage. CRAP = 1·(1−cov)³·1 + 1 = 1 + tiny. With tests: CRAP 1. Behavior identical: runStatus lowercases; the same five statuses. Add characterization tests for each status + non-matching + null run.

Note: `activeRunMatchesTicket` uses isActiveRun? Actually `detectDuplicateRuns`/`activeRunMatchesTicket` — tests exist but isActiveRun itself has 0% coverage. I'll add direct tests.

### 3. `cacheToReleases.action` (CC 31, cov 86%)
Extract pure helpers:
- `resolveTicketKey(params)` — the `params.ticket ? params : (params.jobParams || params)` + ticket key parse. Pure.
- `skipped(reason)` build helper? The skip decisions: no ticketKey → skip; no config → skip; no assets → skip; no artefactRepo → skip. Each has console output + return. Extract `skipIfNotRunnable(params)` returning `{ ok: false, reason, message } | { ok: true, ... }`? Something like `validateRunPreconditions(params, customParams)` pure decide helper.
- The asset loop: extract `postAssetPrComment(...)`? That calls scm (configLoader.createScm) — impure but extractable as a unit; "same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order" — as long as the calls happen identically. Extracting a function keeps the calls in the same order.
- `buildAssetResult` / `processAsset(asset, ...)` → `{ name, result }` plus releaseUrl extraction.

The matching-PR filter is pure: `findMatchingPr(prs, ticketKey)` — extractable pure helper.

Let me plan `action` structure post-refactor:

```js
function action(params) {
   try {
       var prepared = prepareCacheRun(params);       // pure decide: ticketKey/customParams/config/assets/artefactRepo/scmProvider/releaseConfig
       if (!prepared.ok) { log+return skip }
       ... console.log lines ...
       for each asset: results.push(processAsset(...))
       return finalize
   } catch (e) { ... }
``

Careful: console.log lines with buildTag/buildReleaseName are between preparation and loop. Keep the exact same console output.

Actually, let me carefully restructure with pure helpers, keeping all console.* calls and their exact text/order. The `try/catch` must remain in `action` (behavior: errors → `{success:false,error}`).

Extracted pure helpers:
1. `resolveRunContext(params)` → returns `{ skip: {success:true,skipped:true}, ticketKey, customParams, config, assets, artefactRepo, projectConfig, scmProvider, releaseConfig }` or `{skip:...}` — but console.warn/log differ per reason; the helper can return `{ok, reason}` and action logs. Reason strings: 'no-ticket', 'not-configured', 'no-assets', 'no-artefact-repo'. Hmm, but that changes `action` complexity little. Let me count target CC for action: try/catch adds 1? Cyclomatic complexity counts each `if`, `for`, `&&`, `||`, ternary, catch.crap4js complexity.js — let me check what it counts. Actually let me look at complexity.js to know exactly how CC is computed so I can hit CC ≤ 8.

2. `assetRunnable(asset)` — `{fromFolder && name}` check.
3. `findMatchingPr(prs, ticketKey)` — pure.
4. `prCommentBody(asset, ticketKey, scmProvider, releaseUrl)` — pure build (uses resolveTemplate — that's from releaseArtefacts, pure?).
5. `sumarizeResults(results, assets)` — pure.

messages.preview: The formula is `CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC` — so with 100% coverage, CRAP = CC. Let me check exactly how the fork counts cyclomatic complexity.

blocks.text:
The formula is:

CRAP = CC² · (1 − coverage)³ + CC

- `isActiveRun`: CC 5, cov 0 → 25·1 + 5 = 30 ✓
- `classify`: CC 34, cov 0.959 → 1156·(0.041)³ + 34 = 1156·0.000689 + 34 = 0.0797 + 34 = 34.08 ≈ 34.1 ✓
- `orphanedRunChecks`: CC 23, cov 1 → 0 + 23 = 23 ✓
- `collectArtifacts`: CC 8, cov 0.261 → 64·(0.739)³ + 8 = 64·0.4036 + 8 = 25.8 + 8 = 33.8 ✓
- `action` (cacheToReleases): CC 31, cov 0.860 → 961·(0.14)³ + 31 = 961·0.002744 + 31 = 2.637+31 = 33.6 ≈ 33.7 ✓

So the target: CRAP ≤ 8 for each named function.
- With 100% coverage, CRAP = CC. So a function with CC ≤ 8 fully covered gives CRAP ≤ 8. 
- `classify` at CC 34 → need extraction + 100% coverage of each helper; `classify` itself must drop to CC ≤ 8 with 100% coverage (CRAP = CC ≤ 8).

The hard floor is 30 (never above baseline).

Plan per function:

### 1. `checkRunZombies.classify` (CC 34)
Extract the per-check-run decision into pure helpers, e.g.:
- `classifyLinkedRun(cr, runId, resolveRun, nowMs, graceMs)` → verdict object `{kind, zombie}` — handles probe error, no-run, active, completed/canceled/concluded/propagation-lag/odd.
- `classifyUnlinkedRun(cr, nowMs, staleMs)` → verdict — stale-no-runner vs live.
- maybe `completedRunVerdict(state, runId, cr, nowMs, graceMs)`.

Then `classify` becomes: iterate checkRuns, call `isPendingCheckRun` → settled; runIdOf; dispatch to helpers; tally counters. Target CC ≤ 8.

Each helper fully covered by tests. The existing test suite (49 tests) already covers classify thoroughly at 95.9%. After extraction, helpers must be 100% covered. Which branch is currently uncovered? Coverage 95.9% on classify. Let me find uncovered statements: probably `out.live++ // completed without a conclusion` (odd case) or `lag !== null && lag >= 0 && lag <= graceMs` false-negative branch... I'll check coverage detail after refactor. New tests must cover every branch of the helpers.

### 2. `dfManager.isActiveRun` (CC 5, cov 0)
0% coverage! Rewrite as status lookup:
```js
var ACTIVE_RUN_STATUSES = ['queued', 'pending', 'requested', 'waiting', 'in_progress'];
function isActiveRun(run) {
   return ACTIVE_RUN_STATUSES.indexOf(runStatus(run)) !== -1;
}
``
CC becomes 1; CRAP = 1 + 0 = ... CC=1, cov: need coverage. CRAP = 1·(1−cov)³·1 + 1 = 1 + tiny. With tests: CRAP 1. Behavior identical: runStatus lowercases; the same five statuses. Add characterization tests for each status + non-matching + null run.

Note: `activeRunMatchesTicket` uses isActiveRun? Actually `detectDuplicateRuns`/`activeRunMatchesTicket` — tests exist but isActiveRun itself has 0% coverage. I'll add direct tests.

### 3. `cacheToReleases.action` (CC 31, cov 86%)
Extract pure helpers:
- `resolveTicketKey(params)` — the `params.ticket ? params : (params.jobParams || params)` + ticket key parse. Pure.
- `skipped(reason)` build helper? The skip decisions: no ticketKey → skip; no config → skip; no assets → skip; no artefactRepo → skip. Each has console output + return. Extract `skipIfNotRunnable(params)` returning `{ ok: false, reason, message } | { ok: true, ... }`? Something like `validateRunPreconditions(params, customParams)` pure decide helper.
- The asset loop: extract `postAssetPrComment(...)`? That calls scm (configLoader.createScm) — impure but extractable as a unit; "same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order" — as long as the calls happen identically. Extracting a function keeps the calls in the same order.
- `buildAssetResult` / `processAsset(asset, ...)` → `{ name, result }` plus releaseUrl extraction.

The matching-PR filter is pure: `findMatchingPr(prs, ticketKey)` — extractable pure helper.

Let me plan `action` structure post-refactor:

```js
function action(params) {
   try {
       var prepared = prepareCacheRun(params);       // pure decide: ticketKey/customParams/config/assets/artefactRepo/scmProvider/releaseConfig
       if (!prepared.ok) { log+return skip }
       ... console.log lines ...
       for each asset: results.push(processAsset(...))
       return finalize
   } catch (e) { ... }

Hmm, CRAP formula: CRAP = comp² + comp * (1 - coverage). For CC 34, cov 95.9%: 1156 + 34*0.041 = 1157.4 — that's not 34.1.

So crap4js computes differently. Looking at the numbers: `classify` CC 34, CRAP 34.1. `orphanedRunChecks` CC 23, cov 100%, CRAP 23. So when coverage is 100%, CRAP = CC. Let me compute: 34.1 - 34 = 0.1. So the "extra" is 0.1. If CRAP = comp + comp*(1-cov), then extra = 34*0.041 = 1.4. Not 0.1.

Maybe coverage here is a weighted thing... The standard CRAP formula: CRAP = min(comp² + comp(1-cov), comp²·100 + comp). Actually CRAPmin = comp² and CRAPmax = comp²(1-cov) + comp... no.

Standard: CRAP = comp^2 + comp*(1-coverage). With comp=34, cov=0.959: 1156 + 1.394 = 1157. Max value (cov=0): comp²·100 + comp = 115600+34. Hmm.

But observed: CC 34 → CRAP 34.1; CC 5 cov 0 → CRAP 30?? That contradicts everything: with CC 5 and cov 0, standard CRAP = 25 + 5 = 30. Yes! Standard formula gives 30 for CC5/cov0. And for CC 5 cov 100% → 25. But `orphanedRunChecks` CC 23 cov 100% → CRAP 23, whereas standard gives 529.

- orphanedRunChecks: 23 + 0 = 23 ✓ (cov 100%)
- classify: 34 + 34·0.041·5 = 34 + 6.97 = 40.97 ✗ (should be 34.1)

Hmm no. Let me check: maybe the cov% for classify is not exactly 95.9 (rounded). CRAP 34.1 = 34 + 34·(1−x)·k → 0.1 = 34·(1−x)·k. If k=5, (1−x) = 0.000588 → x = 99.94%? Displayed as 95.9%? No.

The current coverage is 95.9% — some branch is uncovered (CRAP 34.1 with CC 34 means coverage ~95.9%... CRAP = comp² + comp(1-cov) = 1156 + 34*0.041 = 1157? No wait.

Hmm, CRAP formula: CRAP = comp² + comp * (1 - coverage). For CC 34, cov 95.9%: 1156 + 34*0.041 = 1157.4 — that's not 34.1.

So crap4js computes differently. Looking at the numbers: `classify` CC 34, CRAP 34.1. `orphanedRunChecks` CC 23, cov 100%, CRAP 23. So when coverage is 100%, CRAP = CC. Let me compute: 34.1 - 34 = 0.1. So the "extra" is 0.1. If CRAP = comp + comp*(1-cov), then extra = 34*0.041 = 1.4. Not 0.1.

Maybe coverage here is a weighted thing... The standard CRAP formula: CRAP = min(comp² + comp(1-cov), comp²·100 + comp). Actually CRAPmin = comp² and CRAPmax = comp²(1-cov) + comp... no.

Standard: CRAP = comp^2 + comp*(1-coverage). With comp=34, cov=0.959: 1156 + 1.394 = 1157. Max value (cov=0): comp²·100 + comp = 115600+34. Hmm.

But observed: CC 34 → CRAP 34.1; CC 5 cov 0 → CRAP 30?? That contradicts everything: with CC 5 and cov 0, standard CRAP = 25 + 5 = 30. Yes! Standard formula gives 30 for CC5/cov0. And for CC 5 cov 100% → 25. But `orphanedRunChecks` CC 23 cov 100% → CRAP 23, whereas standard gives 529.

Hmm wait, maybe the report's "CC" column is not the cyclomatic complexity used in the CRAP formula. Maybe it reports "CC" = crap/... hmm.

- classify: CC 34, cov 95.9%, CRAP 34.1

- orphanedRunChecks: 23 + 0 = 23 ✓ (cov 100%)
- classify: 34 + 34·0.041·5 = 34 + 6.97 = 40.97 ✗ (should be 34.1)

Hmm no. Let me check: maybe the cov% for classify is not exactly 95.9 (rounded). CRAP 34.1 = 34 + 34·(1−x)·k → 0.1 = 34·(1−x)·k. If k=5, (1−x) = 0.000588 → x = 99.94%? Displayed as 95.9%? No.

A CallExpression argument function expression isn't any of those... let me check how the walker treats it — the HANDLERS list: FunctionDeclaration, ClassMethod, VariableDeclarator, AssignmentExpression, ObjectMethod, ObjectProperty, Class*, ExportDefault... For other nodes there's a generic traversal (default handler descends into children). So the test() callback function expression — when the walker reaches a FunctionExpression NOT in an entry position... does it create an entry? The empirical evidence: test-file functions in the reports are only named ones (makeSmAgent 61 etc.) — and makeSmAgent IS a top-level FunctionDeclaration. My new test files' suites: `suite('isActiveRun', function() {...})` — anonymous function argument → NOT an entry, but its complexity counts toward... nothing (module scope has no entry) — OR toward the enclosing top-level `function loadCacheToReleases`? No — they're siblings.

Wait — but the BEFORE report showed `loadCacheToReleases CC 14` — the mock property functions counted toward it (nested). And `makeSmAgent` (a named FunctionDeclaration) = own entry. What about the complexity of anonymous function at module top level (suite callback)? It must count into SOME entry or be dropped. Looking at the walker: for CallExpression the generic traversal descends into arguments; reaching the FunctionExpression node — there's no handler for plain FunctionExpression in entry position... Actually FUNCTION_LIKE = FunctionExpression + ArrowFunctionExpression are in SKIP-ish handling? The comment says "Lambda/arrow bodies count TOWARDS the enclosing function (we descend into them when computing the parent's complexity)". For ENTRY detection, the handlers only push entries for the named shapes; the generic walk just descends. So a module-level anonymous suite callback's complexity is attributed to... nothing (no entry) — harmless.

But WAIT — then why was `loadCacheToReleases` CC 14 and the mock property functions also reported separately (uploadArtefact 2)? ObjectProperty handler pushes an entry for the property function AND... the complexity of loadCacheToReleases counted them too? That contradicts "the parent doesn't descend into entries". Hmm — unless the ObjectProperty entries were NOT pushed (babel AST: `{ buildTag: function() {} }` is a Property with value FunctionExpression — handler `ObjectProperty` checks `FUNCTION_LIKE.has(node.value.type)` → pushes entry named by key). So buildTag etc. SHOULD be separate entries — but the before-report did NOT show buildTag/resolveTemplate entries in test_cacheToReleases.js (it showed only loadCacheToReleases 14, resolveArtefactRepository 7!, uploadArtefact 2, resolveTemplate 2, buildTag 2, buildReleaseName 2, listPrs 2, addComment 1, loadProjectConfig 2, createScm 1...). And ALSO `loadCacheToReleases 14`?! So BOTH: the property functions are entries AND their complexity counted toward loadCacheToReleases. Wait — that can't be... 14 = sum of the property functions' complexities: buildTag 2 + buildReleaseName 2 + resolveTemplate 2 + resolveArtefactRepository 7 + uploadArtefact 2 + listPrs 2 + addComment 1 + loadProjectConfig 2 + createScm 1 = 21 ≠ 14. Hmm. 14 - 1(base) = 13. Whatever the exact rule (maybe it descends into ObjectProperty values but doesn't descend into nested NAMED...), empirically my fix worked: extractMethods now shows no CC > 8 in the file.
